messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test in `TypeUtilsTest.testGetTypeArguments()` shows that `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class)` does not return the expected size of 2 for the type variable assignments. According to the test, the returned map should contain two type arguments assigned to `This`'s type parameters.

Looking at the `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>)` method family:
- The main entry forwards to `getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>, Map)` which dispatches on the runtime type of the first argument (Class, ParameterizedType, etc.).
- For Class arguments, `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)` checks if the classes are assignable and prepares a mutable map.
- Critically, around line 675: `if (cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 || toClass.equals(cls)) { return typeVarAssigns; }`
  - This means if the source class `cls` has type parameters of its own (i.e., it is generic), or the target class is equal to `cls`, it will immediately return the current collected map without further traversing the inheritance or resolving more type arguments.
- Only if this condition is false (no type parameters and not the target) it recurses on a closest parent type.

This is suspicious especially when a partially-assigned or generic class is involved. It seems to short-circuit the resolution as soon as it encounters a generic class (with type parameters) without advancing to resolve mappings for superclasses or interfaces. The test input `Other.class, This.class` likely involves these complex generics.

In contrast, the `getTypeArguments(ParameterizedType, ...)` method does continue to accumulate and resolve type parameter mappings up the class/interface hierarchy by recursive calls.

Hence, the bug is that `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)` prematurely stops and returns the current assignments if the class has type parameters, without continuing to traverse the inheritance chain to fully resolve the mappings. This causes partial or missing mappings for partially-parameterized types.

In summary, the code does not correctly handle partially assigned generics in `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)`, missing further inheritance traversal and thus missing some type argument mappings. This explains the failing test that expects 2 mappings but gets fewer.

Recent bug reports do not appear relevant to this generic type argument resolution issue.

Key lines involved:
- `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)`: line 675 stop condition on type parameters.
- Recursive inheritance traversal missing due to this short-circuit.

A fix would likely involve removing or adjusting this short-circuit so that type argument resolution continues up the superclass and interface hierarchy even when the class itself has type parameters.

This diagnosis fully explains the failure seen in the test `testGetTypeArguments()` for the `Other.class, This.class` case.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
